# Mr. Georg von Welling's
# A MAGO-CABBALISTIC AND THEOSOPHICAL WORK,
<note>original Latin: "Opus Mago-Cabbalisticum et Theosophicum"</note>

->wherein<-
->the origin, nature, properties, and use<-
->of<-

# Salt, Sulfur
->and<-
# M E R C U R Y,
<note>In alchemy, these three substances—Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—are known as the "Tria Prima" or three primes, believed to be the fundamental components of all material things.</note>

described in three parts, and along with many very strange mathematical, theosophical, magical, and mystical matters, the generation of metals and minerals is also proven from the foundation of nature; together with the master key of the entire work, and many curious <term>mago-cabbalistic</term><note>A term combining "magic" and "Kabbalah," referring to a mystical tradition that seeks to understand the universe through divine names, numbers, and symbols.</note> figures. To which is further added: A small treatise on Divine Wisdom; and a special appendix of several very rare and precious chemical pieces.

# Preface
## of the Editor.

->Beloved Reader!<-

With this, we present to you the **Mago-Cabbalistic and Theosophical Work** <note>original: "Opus Mago-Cabbalisticum & Theosophicum"; a foundational 18th-century text by Georg von Welling concerning alchemy, salt, and sacred mysteries.</note> in its complete state, which has been long desired by many. It is our heartfelt wish that it might serve you with great benefit and much edification! We also venture to assure you that the late author <note>original: "seel. Autor" — "seel." is an abbreviation for "selig," meaning "blessed" or "of blessed memory," used to refer to a person who has passed away.</note> brought forth and testified to much good and many precious truths within these pages, regarding both natural and spiritual or Divine things. However, for that very reason, we do not demand that you hold it in higher regard than is proper, nor that you accept anything without examination. No; rather, we are quite happy to let the saying of the Apostle Paul stand here, where he says: **1 Thessalonians 5:21. Test all things; hold fast to what is good.** For just as no wheat grows from the earth without having its chaff with it;

<summary>The editor introduces a complete edition of a significant mystical and alchemical treatise, encouraging the reader to study its truths while exercising spiritual discernment.</summary>
<keywords>preface, Mago-Cabbalistic, theosophy, spiritual discernment, alchemy, Georg von Welling, 1 Thessalonians 5:21</keywords>

--- Page 18 ---
<meta>This page continues the Preface from the previous leaf, completing the metaphor of wheat and chaff used to describe the mixture of profound truth and human imperfection within the text.</meta>

so we also believe that the good **core-truths** <note>original: "Kern-Wahrheiten"</note> of this book are still provided or mixed with some chaff and prickly awns <note>original: "Ahnen"; the beard or bristles found on spikes of grain.</note>, which a sensible person will easily know how to blow away and make use of the good little grains for his own benefit. And so, we hand it over entirely to everyone for their own examination and judgment, without taking any responsibility for it in the slightest.

Regarding the **Appendix**, we have had it translated from the **Latin manuscripts** <note>original: "Lateinischen Manuscriptis"</note> which a good friend shared with us for this purpose, and have had them printed with the work in the hope that they will also serve someone; not that we sought thereby to infect anyone with the **gold-fever** <note>original: "Goldsucht"; a term used to describe the greedy or obsessive pursuit of physical wealth through alchemy rather than spiritual enlightenment.</note> that is already rampant everywhere: No, rather we wish from our hearts that all people, instead of gold, might seek and find GOD.

But because we are nonetheless aware that every human being gladly strives and searches for something, we also consider it permissible to strive with due modesty after such a **noble art** <note>A common reference to the "Royal Art" of alchemy or the pursuit of the Philosopher's Stone.</note>, of which we know for certain that GOD grants it to some whom He recognizes as faithful to Him, and who also walk the right path to attain it and humbly ask Him for it. However, we do not present such small works as being higher than they are, and we leave them, just like the rest, entirely to everyone’s examination and judgment. With this, we heartily commend the beloved reader to the grace of GOD.

->Given at Homburg vor der Höhe,<-
->the 7th of January, 1735.<-

C. S. <note>These initials likely belong to Christoph Schütz (1689–1750), the editor and publisher associated with this edition of Welling's work.</note>

<summary>The editor concludes the preface by defending the inclusion of alchemical manuscripts while warning against greed, ultimately entrusting the reader to discern the book's spiritual "wheat" from its "chaff."</summary>
<keywords>discernment, gold-fever, Latin manuscripts, Homburg vor der Höhe, Christoph Schütz, spiritual alchemy, 1735</keywords>

# Preface
## Of the *Author*.

->Sincere and gentle reader!<-

Know that the prompting of a good friend led us quite wonderfully to the *composition* <term>the act of writing and arranging the work</term> of this work; not that it should be presented openly to the world, but as something from which we might always draw occasion for our secret and intimate *conversation* <term>in this period, the term referred to a shared way of life and the private exchange of ideas among a close circle</term>.

But because the first part of this work came to light <note>i.e., was published or leaked</note> against our will, we did not want to leave it alone, but rather decided to accompany it with the second and third parts; doubting not that this work—since it is now *complete* <note>original: "complet"</note> and the first part has been *corrected* <note>original: "corrigiret"</note> by us for its frequent errors—will be dear and pleasant. In this labor, we seek no glory or thanks, except for the reader's satisfaction, and that the reader might likewise recognize and find within it that which the wisdom of **GOD** has communicated to us; just as we hold ourselves certain that this work will give a holy pleasure to **God**-devoted souls. And so, a lover of *Magical Kabbalah* <note>original: "Mago-Cabbalæ"; a tradition combining Jewish mysticism with Hermetic philosophy</note> and *Theosophy* <note>original: "Theosophiæ"; here referring to "Divine Wisdom" or the mystical study of God's nature</note> [will] our intention

<summary>In this preface, the author reveals that the book was originally intended only for private circulation among friends, but it is being published in full because a partial, error-filled version was leaked. The author expresses a desire to share divine wisdom with fellow seekers of the "Magical Kabbalah" rather than seeking personal fame.</summary>

<keywords>preface, authorship, private circulation, correction of errors, Divine Wisdom, Magical Kabbalah, Theosophy, 18th-century literature</keywords>

--- Page 20 ---
<meta>This page continues the Preface from the previous page, completing the sentence regarding the reader's ability to recognize the author's intent.</meta>

easily recognize and understand that our intention is not directed toward teaching someone how to make gold. Instead, our aim is toward something far higher: namely, how Nature may be seen and recognized as coming from **GOD**, and how **GOD** may be seen and recognized within Nature; and further, how from this knowledge, the true and pure service of the *creature* <note>in this context, "creature" refers to all created things, including humans, animals, and minerals</note> flows as a rightful *sacrifice of thanks* <note>original: "Danck-Opffer"</note> toward the Creator.

In this, however, a sincere lover of true, nature-conforming <term>Chymistry</term> <note>the early modern precursor to chemistry that included spiritual and alchemical dimensions</note> will find great guidance for walking the true path of Nature and avoiding the paths of error. Indeed, we have not written so obscurely that a sincere and diligent soul should fail to see what we have aimed for. 

The <term>Kabbalistic Characters</term> <note>original: "Cabbalistische Characteres"; mystical symbols used to represent divine or cosmic forces</note>, which we have employed here and there in this work for certain reasons, will not be at all difficult for one practiced in this science to decipher. Furthermore, let no one be surprised that we have used *Chemical Signs*, *Terms* <note>original: "Terminorum"</note>, and modes of speech; for by these means, we can present what we wish to indicate much more clearly, distinctly, and comprehensibly—as well as more in accordance with nature—than with *metaphysical terms* <note>original: "Metaphysischen Terminis"</note>. 

With this, we then conclude this preface and hand over this work to the righteous judgment of the enlightened and **GOD**-devoted reader.

January 4th, 1721.

The Author.

<meta>catchword: Sum-</meta>

<summary>The author concludes the preface by clarifying that the book's goal is spiritual enlightenment and the recognition of God in Nature rather than the literal creation of gold. He explains his use of Kabbalistic and chemical symbols as a way to describe natural truths more clearly than abstract philosophical language.</summary>
<keywords>alchemy vs spirituality, Nature as divine revelation, Kabbalistic symbols, chemical terminology, sacrifice of thanks, 1721, early modern science</keywords>

# THE MAGO-KABBALISTIC WORK
## Part One,
->dealing with<-
## S A L T.

### Chapter I.
### On the Origin of Common Salt.

->§. 1.<-

It is quite surprising how many opinions have been produced regarding the origin and first generation of salt (that is, common kitchen salt, which is the true source of all other salts, by whatever name they may be called). This has been done by both the learned and the unlearned, and one might almost say there are as many minds or opinions on this point as there are heads. Yet, in truth, this is not one of the least significant matters regarding the beginnings of natural things; rather, one might almost say it is the first and foremost in the economy of this entire world. It is therefore well worthy of being weighed with better reflection. We should set aside preconceived notions and what this or that scholar has most learnedly written speculatively in his idle study, without true <term>practice</term> <note>original: "Praxin"</note> and thorough investigation through <term>arduous laboratory work</term> <note>original: "mühseliges Laboriren"</note>. Instead, we should strive to inquire into its true origin and material generation—as we later grasp and feel it, and enjoy it in food and drink—through true observation consistent with nature. For simply distilling a <term>spirit</term> <note>In alchemy, a "spirit" refers to the volatile essence or vapor extracted from a substance through distillation.</note> from this or that salt is by no means the way to judge its true origin and essence. Nor is it sufficient to say that it was initially created as a material and bodily substance by God the Almighty and stored in the <term>Great World-Ocean</term> <note>original: "Welt-Meer"</note> as a general treasure chest, and from there [leads] through underground passages, as if through veins, throughout the entire globe—

<insert>
Cassel, the 20th, Michael Büsch <unclear>??</unclear> 22 June 1771
</insert>

<summary>This page introduces Salt as the foundational element of the physical world, critiquing theoretical scholars and emphasizing the need for practical laboratory investigation into its origins. The author dismisses the simple idea that salt was merely stored in the ocean by God, promising a deeper explanation of its creation.</summary>
<keywords>salt, alchemy, laboratory practice, origins of matter, world-ocean, Kabbalah, Michael Büsch, Cassel</keywords>

--- Page 24 ---
<meta>This page continues the first chapter's investigation into the nature of salt. The previous page established that salt is the fundamental principle of the world and criticized purely theoretical scholarship in favor of practical laboratory observation.</meta>

...[that it] is led, and here and there reveals itself through springs, from which the body of salt is then separated from its water by fire and presented to us.

->§. 2.<-

It is undeniable among all rational men that salt, as we enjoy it, is brought to us from the great sea through subterranean passages and fissures, and is separated from its wateriness by boiling; however, this does not yet prove its true origin in the slightest.

->§. 3.<-

And so that all foreign opinions on this point may be set aside, and the path may be opened to the truth from the foundation of nature, we will first consider salt according to its material form and figure as it appears before our eyes. We generally have three kinds of it, which are basically one and the same: spring salt, rock salt, and sea salt. All three are essentially the same in their nature and figure, although they differ slightly in shape when not separated from their foreign parts. A fourth kind could also be added here, and not unfairly: namely, common earth and mother-salt, the <term>🜔</term> <note>The alchemical symbol for Salt.</note>. Christ, our Savior, says very thoughtfully in Luke 14:34–35: "Salt is a good thing, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what shall it be seasoned? Furthermore, mention was made above that waters from our northern climates, when taken upon sea-vessels under the Ecliptic <note>the path of the sun across the sky</note>, become thick and muddy. However, when brought back to these northern places, they become thin again and as combustible as brandy. This thoroughly proves what we have just stated: namely, that the closer waters are to the Poles, the more **lunar** they are, lacking the **masculine solar seed** with which they are, by contrast, richly impregnated under the Ecliptic. On the other hand, waters at Batavia <note>modern-day Jakarta, Indonesia</note> and other well-situated places in the East Indies, when loaded for the voyage home, are said to remain good throughout the Ecliptic until they reach the fatherland. Thus, our previous discourse is once again powerfully confirmed: namely, the closer waters are to the Ecliptic, the more **solar** they are, and vice versa.

But before we break off here, we must once more take up the previously cited passage from Luke and, with permission, ask what our Savior actually means by these words: "But if the salt has lost its taste, with what shall it be seasoned?" Furthermore, it is useful neither for the land nor for the manure. We fear, however, that because "manure" and similar "filth" are mentioned, such people will take little trouble to fathom these Divine mysteries. We wish, therefore, to seal these secrets with the almost unfathomable words of our Savior when he says: "Salt is a good thing," etc. "No one is good but God alone," etc. "For everyone must be salted with fire, and every sacrifice shall be seasoned with salt. Have salt in yourselves, and have peace with one another." (Mark 9:48–49).

# The First Chapter.

An artful refiner <term>Scheider; a specialist in separating metals or chemical components</term> must know how to assist in this, namely, he must know how to give them the right cooking-fire and water, if he wishes to fix the volatile <note>original: "das Flüchtige figiren"; to turn a substance from a gas or liquid state into a stable, solid form</note> and arrange the separation usefully. The fire must not be unknown to him; and we believe regarding the working-water <note>original: "Uebungs-Wasser"; likely a solvent or acid used in the alchemical process</note> with certainty that it is not that acidic common salt which is necessary for this fixation. Rather, the artist, before he undertakes this work, must well know the sweet alkali of nature <note>original: "süsse Alcalinum der Natur"</note>, and how it is sharpened by the fiery sunbeams. For certainly, whoever does not know this physical salt has not yet experienced the distinction of salts. For the saline working-water of the metallic, animal, and vegetable bodies is a completely different salt than the acidic common salt found in seas, wells, mountains, and in the earth. However, no one here should imagine that we act against our first principle in §. 10, where we said that common salt is the beginning and the end of all things; rather, we confirm this once more. Because the natural salt just mentioned (as the root-stem of the acidic salt found everywhere) is not so visible before our eyes, but rather as it has become physical through the subterranean fire in this great kitchen (the terrestrial globe) and has taken on acidity from the fire-beams or sulfurous vapors (which are themselves nothing but salt), enough has been said for the lovers of truth and wisdom. The fools, however, may understand it as they wish. It is enough that when we speak of the working-water or of the salty water that dissolves all bodies, we speak of salt as we see, touch, and taste it, and which the understanding man can transform at any moment into the natural salt. For it is the very same salt generated by the sun, moon, and stars, of which enough and more has been said before; and thus, no objection will remain among the understanding.

§. 31. Shortly before, we considered that the acidity of our universal salt in this great Earth-kitchen was caused by the sulfurous vapors of the subterranean fire, even in the sea itself, which is likewise not at all free from the exhalations of this subterranean fire. That this is true, coal <note>original: "Stein-Kohlen"; literally "stone-coal," referring to mineral coal mined from the earth</note> shall especially prove to us. For in truth, he who denies that where there is coal, no salt-springs are found, or where salt-springs are found, there is no coal, is quite simple-minded and little practiced or experienced in nature; this requires no proof at all. Therefore, because the salt-veins mostly run deep, the surface and "roof" coals <note>original: "Tage- und Dach-Kohlen"; coal found near the surface</note> have less fixity and utility than the stone, fat, or pitch coals <note>original: "Stein- Fett- oder Pech-Kohlen"; types of high-quality, bituminous coal</note>, as there the erupted sulfur is better fixed and bound by the salt-streams; on the other hand, the salt-veins also take more and more of the sulfur's acidity into themselves...

Furthermore, the work of fire <note>pyro-chemistry or laboratory practice</note> teaches us tangibly that no *body* may be found in nature that cannot be entirely *reduced* to salt, even the most perfect ones, such as *gold* and *silver*.

But alas! Take several thousand pounds of wood and burn it, in such a way that all the smoke and moisture may be captured without any loss. When it is burnt, the smallest part will be ash, in which resides a fixed sulfurous salt. Leach this well <note>to dissolve the soluble salts out of the ash using water</note>, place it in a suitable vessel, and pour as much of the captured *liquor* <note>the condensed smoke and moisture</note> onto it as is needed to moisten it. Seal the vessel and let it stand in proper *digestion* <note>The process of maintaining gentle, steady heat to encourage chemical change</note>. Thus, this moisture will truly *coagulate* and become *fixed* within the salt—that is, it will turn into salt itself. *Continue* this with patience, and you will, without any dispute, have all your captured moisture *fixed* and *congealed* back into a true salt. This is the first part.

But here we must necessarily look about us and resist a whole troop of *sophists*, grimy coal-smutters <note>a derogatory term for "puffers" or false alchemists who merely burn coal without understanding theory</note>, and destroyers of the works of God, who all unanimously have so much to say, chatter, and scream about the deaf, dead, leached-out ash, which they call *Terra damnata* <note>Latin: "damned earth"; the worthless residue left after chemical extraction</note>. They ask: where does this remain? Does it also become salt? Does this not go entirely against nature? The answer, however, is: Yes, you fools! If you knew nature and her ways, you would know what your *Terra damnata* was in the beginning, and that all things are to be brought back into their first essence. You would then not rage so cruelly against nature and destroy her, but would learn to recognize that all *bodies*, from the beginning and progress of their growth until their perfection, may be brought back to their beginning and first original state by that very same path. All of this we allowed to flow into a mass and scattered about one and a half pounds of it into a clarified pan full of brine standing in the boil. We let it boil down thoroughly, and thus, from the red brine—full of "wild water" and drawn with bucket and rope—there precipitated an exceedingly magnificent, white, and durable salt with good profit. No moisture could harm this salt; rather, it became like a stone and surpassed all other known common cooking salts in pleasantness and sharpness. 

After these times, however, the <term>shareholders</term> <note>original: *Gewerck*; the members of a mining or salt-working corporation</note> of that same work, to whom this technique had not been revealed, endeavored to maintain their profit through <term>graduation</term> <note>the process of concentrating brine by letting it evaporate naturally while trickling over brushwood towers</note>. Rather, the lover of truth should know that the **lunar salt** is so internally united with the **water** <note>original symbol: $\nabla$</note> that they cannot be separated by boiling except with great difficulty, as can be seen more perfectly at the end of Chapter 1 and in other places. Therefore, our **precipitation** is nothing other than a complete separation of these **heavenly influences** (the **solar** ones <note>original symbol: $\odot$</note>) **from the matrix** <note>original: *à Matrice*</note>, namely from the **water**, with which it is so intimately united; for as all our preceding discourse has proven, both are of one origin and essence in their innermost being. 

Thus, the actual effect of this **precipitation** is the complete separation of the salt from the water, so that the water evaporates away much faster and easier, and leaves behind the salt perfectly beautiful, hard, and well-qualified. It also prevents even the slightest bit from escaping within the delicate water-vapor, as if into the air. Consequently, one requires much less wood and time for the true boiling, and obtains a much more magnificent and far greater quantity of salt than would otherwise be obtained in any other way or manner. [seu] absolutus"</note>, but is only to be called a movement according to the force of its weight and following the said lines. For pure and absolute motion consists in the free will of living creatures, which we wish to prove clearly to those unlearned in mathematics and physics <note>original: "Mathesi & Physicis"</note>.

Given is the surface <note>original: "superficies"</note> *s. q.*, see Figure Number 12, which is entirely horizontal and level, so that it tilts in no direction. A perfectly round sphere placed upon it, no matter the location, lies entirely motionless and still, according to its diameter or perpendicular *e. a.* upon the point of rest *a.*, which is also the center of gravity; this may be quite well understood by any reasonable person. It is then also clear as day and incontestable that if one imagines a perpendicular *a. z.* through this horizon *s. q.*, rising with perfect equality and unity with the diameter of the sphere *a. e.*, then the sphere *b. c. d. a.* must rest just as still, stiff, and immobile upon the perpendicular *a. z.* at the point of rest *a.* as it does upon the horizon *s. q.*. The same condition of rest applies to the cube <note>original: "Cubo"</note> *h. g. i. k.* on the very same horizon *s. q.* and the perpendicular *n. l.* at the point of rest *l.*, which is the center of gravity. How easily a sphere weighing many hundreds of pounds may be moved, and how difficult by contrast an equally heavy cube is to move upon such a level horizon common to both, requires no proof, but is known even to children.

Secondly, if the surface *W. So it is clear as day that, due to the concentrated weight *f. e. c. a.*, the sphere can no longer rest at *f.* on the perpendicular *f. c.*, but will roll away and hasten toward point *X.*. Instead, because all rest has been taken from it, it hurries violently downward along the perpendicular a. h. For since nature tolerates no empty space <note>original: "leeren Raum"; a reference to the classical principle of 'horror vacui'</note>, and such a thing can neither be proven nor even conceived, the place a. Therefore, the movement of the body, although caused by its own weight, is not pure, but mixed. # The Third Chapter.

Since the creation on the sixth day ended with the human being, whom Moses or the holy text calls ADAM, then the conclusion must be made, without any objection, firm and irrefutable: that man must be that perfect thing of which we have treated from the beginning until now. Indeed, he is not only that perfect thing, but something far greater and more perfect, in that his eternally living spirit was communicated to him directly from the eternal light (Genesis 2:7), so that he himself is a tiny spark of the living Divinity. Whoever has ears here, let him hear, and also read with the highest attention the first chapters of Genesis and these three chapters of our description; then he will in truth find and see more than he ever believed. To set everything down here word for word, however, might almost be interpreted as a great and impudent folly on our part. So much has already been said clearly here and there that it is almost unjustifiable; yet this is our comfort: that he to whom the light of the Most High does not shine must be blind even at high noon.

But let man learn to know himself; then, from his entire being, he will judge each and every creature, both visible and invisible, and nothing will remain hidden or covered from him. Even the four separate <term>Principles or secondary qualities</term> <note>original: "Principia oder qualitates secundariæ"</note>, commonly called the <term>Elements</term> <note>original: "Elementa"</note>, will be entirely discovered and revealed to him with all their creatures—which are commonly invisible to us—of which we shall treat further in the third part. Yes, Heaven and Hell, light and darkness, will be perfectly discovered and revealed to him; he will see with firm and irrefutable truth and be fully able to understand that the most deadened body <note>original: "Corpus"</note> can be perfectly restored again and made eternally stable. These latter words might well give offense to one or another inexperienced person, but that shall not hinder us, as it nonetheless is and remains an eternal truth.

From this, man will be able to perfectly see and conclude how, after the determined times of the eternities, every creature involved in darkness—that is, in the dross or horror—shall be overturned again and transposed into the spiritual <term>mercurial life</term> <note>A state of spiritual fluidity and transformation associated with the alchemical Mercury</note>, in which henceforth nothing can work but Spirit and Light. Therefore, O Man! learn above all to know yourself rightly and well, and it will not be hidden from you what that is which the Philosophers call their <term>Mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, but Moses calls <term>Fire</term> <note>original symbol: Δ (Delta/Fire)</note>, that is, <term>Sun and Mercury</term> <note>original symbols: ☉ and ☿</note>, but which we have called by a common, intelligible word: <term>Salt</term>. You will understand what is said in Jeremiah 10:13: *He makes the lightnings into rain;* which words certainly intend to say something more than the common interpreters imagine with their glossing. In short, it is well to consider why man is called the little world (<term>Microcosm</term> <note>original: "Microcolmus", a common variant of Microcosmus</note>)? And since we ourselves are what we seek, it is only right that we make the beginning in and on ourselves.

## Concerning the Primordial World.

The world, of which God—as it were—ordained and created the Son of the Morning <note>original: "Sohn der Morgenröthe," a traditional title for Lucifer before his fall</note> to be the ruler from the majesty of the Most Holy. The eternal Divine Glory, however, ruled and governed this lower world with all its circles through the seven great and mighty spirits of His most holy throne. Thus, through SACHARIEL <note>In various mystical traditions, Sachariel is an archangel associated with Jupiter or the outpouring of divine light</note>, the first influence of Divine Light passed into this lower spirit-world. This gentle and quiet movement of Divine Light would have continued through these great spirits in their order—as it stood then—to this lower world in an unceasing succession with the infinite Divine Glory, had not the Son of the Morning become apostate through pride, thereby causing Divine Justice to cast him out and throw his glorious spirit-world into the confusion of this earthly one.

(namely the throne of the Son of the Morning) was the mirror in which <term>diametrically</term> <note>original: "e Diametro," meaning directly across or in a straight line</note> the rays of the holy Divine Light were concentrated; from there, this holy Divine Light returned (by reflection) and radiated into the remaining circles of his mighty hosts C. D. E. down to the circle of the Sons of God—see Genesis 6:2, Job 1:6, also Chapter 2:1, and Chapter 38:7—which circle was the last of the world of this Son of the Morning. And so, in the beginning of time, the entire creation existed in perfect, peaceful light, peace, and joy: namely, in the throne of the glory of the living God, which is the seven great and mighty spirits before His most holy countenance, through whom the outflows of His majesty are guided to all others; and this is the first world. Furthermore, from the center and circumferences of the Son of the Morning; and this is the second world. Thirdly, from those twelve circles or choirs of the innumerable spirits and angelic hosts; and this is the third and middle world. ## The First Day’s Work

§. 8. The Holy Spirit continues further in the 3rd verse of Genesis 1 to recount the first separation in this chaos: *Then God said, let there be light, and there was light* etc. This was the first separation, namely the revelation of the light within the darkness, so that from then on the beginnings—from which Almighty God intended to create everything visible and invisible—were visible and recognizable, <note>The author views the first day of creation not just as the appearance of physical light, but as the structural beginning of the entire material and spiritual universe.</note> see Figure Number 56. Furthermore, the text says: *so it became evening, and so it also became morning, the first day.* Now, this day was the first period of 24 hours, as clearly shines forth from the contrast with the fourth day’s work, on which the sun and moon were created, and thus the true night and true day were first created through the orbit of the lights. Because the name "day" is given in the same sense to both this first day and that fourth day, it follows that on this first day—through the power of the revealed light—it was bright in one half-circle (that is, day), and because the coarser and darker elements remained below, it was simultaneously night in the other half-circle. Because nothing created exists or can persist without movement, (as Psalm 74 verse 16 says:
>Yours is the day, yours also is the night: You have prepared both, the light and also the sun,<
) this revealed light and darkness created the same distinction between day and night which the celestial lights created on the fourth day’s work, as is clear and manifest through the words of distinction used by the Holy Spirit through Moses, such as "evening" and "morning." The 3rd verse says: *Let there be light, and there was light* etc. This now was the aforementioned revelation of light and darkness, and furthermore, from this light all heavenly lights and bodies under the firmament—namely of our solar system <note>original: "Sonnen-Systematis"</note>—were created. The 4th verse also says: *And God saw that the light was good, and God made a distinction between the light and darkness.* This distinction, according to the proper understanding of the Hebrew word <note>The author likely refers to the Hebrew root 'badal' (בָּדַל), meaning to divide or separate into distinct parts.</note>, is such that one distinguishes a thing so that each of the separated parts has a particular place without being comprised of the other, see Figure Number 57. In the fifth verse it stands: *And God called the light Day, and the darkness Night.* This then shows us clearly and irrefutably that both the day or the light, as well as the night or the darkness, are two essential things <note>The author argues against the idea that darkness is merely the absence of light, asserting instead that it is a "substantial" or "essential" created thing.</note>, as we have already fully proven above in the first chapter and do not find it necessary to repeat here.

### The Fifth Day’s Work.

§. 30. The creatures of this fifth day’s work were everything that lives in the seas, lakes, rivers, and other waters, as well as in the air; as can be clearly seen in Genesis 1, verses 20 to 23. The <term>mercurial substances</term> <note>In alchemy, Mercury represents the principle of fluidity and life-force</note>, such as all <term>vegetables</term> <note>original: "Vegetabilia"; referring here to all plant life</note>, were the first to be separated or brought forth; after these came everything of a <term>saline substance</term> <note>Salt represents the principle of fixity and body</note>, namely all that which lives in the seas and all other waters, as well as in the air. The <term>sulphurous</term> <note>Sulphur represents the principle of combustibility and soul</note> ones, however, such as all the animals of the earth, appear first on the sixth and final day. All these creatures, fish and birds, were—like the plants—before the fall of man and the curse that followed it, glorious, pure, and perfectly healthy in their substance, being neither predatory nor otherwise inclined to cause harm. After the fall and the curse, however, everything within them was turned inward, and their first pure substance was wrapped and locked away in a coarser essence, so that little of that <term>vital sap</term> <note>original: "Lebens-Saft"; the essential life-giving fluid or quintessence</note> necessary for the preservation of human life can be obtained from them. Here we should perhaps speak further and at some length about the various properties of both fish and birds; both those that live in fresh water and those in salt water, and consequently of all birds. However, everything previously discussed will be passed over by everyone. We wish only to say this: namely, that nothing seems more strange to us than that rational people make so much quarreling and talk about the winter quarters or residence of certain birds, such as swallows, storks, etc., since their origin and creation in Genesis 1, verse 20 is as clear as day. Thus, it is truly and irrefutably concluded that during the winter, the time of their absence, they must have their residence in deep lakes, warm marshes, and similar places; there it remains, and with this we also close this fifth <term>day’s work</term> <note>original: "Tagewerck"; a day's labor or a specific period of creation</note>.

### The Sixth and Final Day’s Work.

§. 31. # The Fifth Chapter.

§. 35. Now we return again to the end of the preceding 33rd §. <note>The author is cross-referencing an earlier section regarding the original state of humanity.</note> where we heard what a glorious creature the man Adam was; in what magnificent light and luster, in perfect alignment with the will of God, and thus in true holiness and righteousness, in indescribable gentle stillness, peace, and joy he stood. When God the Lord had created him so gloriously after His own image and likeness, and had made him a ruler of this entire universe (from which Lucifer had fallen), and had given him Eden as his throne, He commanded him that he should not lust after, much less eat from, the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil, under the unavoidable penalty of temporal and eternal death. In contrast, he was free to enjoy everything else, even the Tree of Life in the midst of the garden, and to rule over all creatures and things above and below his throne.

Earlier in this chapter, there was extensive talk concerning the fall of Lucifer and its cause, and how this seat of Lucifer was changed into this present world, and how the man Adam was created in Lucifer's place to rule and fill this world. Now, when Lucifer saw this glorious creature, Adam, as a king of this mighty machine <note>original: "Machinæ"; a common Baroque metaphor for the complex, divinely-ordered structure of the physical universe.</note> (from which he had been cast out on account of his pride), his wrath and envy were ignited against this man, seeking to drag him out of this great glory into his own ruin and banishment.

Therefore, he dispatched his deputy, the lord and prince of the air, Beelzebub (since Lucifer himself lies locked in the fiery abyss with the chains and bonds of darkness until the day of final judgment), to incite the man Adam against God’s will and command. He took his opportunity with the man because he saw him alone; he showed or pointed out to him all the kingdoms of this world, suggesting what use all of this was to him if he were so alone. On the other hand, if he would seek to multiply himself into countless millions, then he would truly be able to rule over this world. He suggested that Adam could accomplish this by his own power, as such a mighty king of his own property (this great universe), according to his own will.

And so he enticed the man to lust within himself and after his own great glory against his Creator, and to conceive disobedience against the eternal God in his imagination. He sought after a species <note>original: "Specie"; here referring to a physical form or method of reproduction separate from the divine order.</note> through which he could release his power and multiplication, and occupy this world by his own authority, and thus set himself against his God and King. In this, Satan represented to him that as an immortal spirit, breathed out directly from God, he was eternally immortal and could suffer no transience or death. Through this, sin was effectively, yet spiritually, conceived in Adam.

# The Fifth Chapter.

(As the former ruler of this earthly or animal world,) <note>The author refers to Lucifer/Satan's status before his fall.</note> that this being perceived the **imagination** <note>In this context, "imagination" refers to the creative or formative power of the soul.</note> of the **Woman** to be much more watery, and not as fiery and steadfast as that of the **Man**, and therefore more easily moved to desire all forms of lusts, even within herself, and to radiate into them. Now first arises a very difficult question: what kind of animal was the serpent? Also, was it the Devil himself, or did the Devil only speak through it, using it merely as a **tool**? Truly, there are more **opinions** on this point than there are religions, factions, and sects; and to tell the truth, this text is one of the most important, and it cannot be easily explained through wisdom founded upon human dogmas. The text mentions **Satan** by not a single letter, but rather an animal called the **Serpent**, more cunning than all the beasts of the field, which was also cursed by God the Lord above all beasts of the field (because it seduced humanity) to go upon its **belly** and eat **earth** all the days of its life (Genesis 3:14). From this it is clear that this animal, because it was henceforth to go upon its belly, must have been created differently and must have had feet. It must have been an excellent and beautiful animal, with which the Woman became so infatuated. That it was able to enter **Eden** is shown by the text as clear as day and requires no explanation; it is thus well worthy of the question: what kind of creature was it then? 

Such a thing cannot be clearly seen from the literal letter of the Holy Scripture; what the **Rabbis** and others dream about it is far too absurd to be cited here, and other opinions might not be much better. Therefore, the truth must be drawn from the circumstances of this history. The text says in Genesis 3:1 that the serpent **spoke** to the woman: *"Has God indeed said..."* etc. These words show as clear as day that an extensive conversation (or a disputation) with the woman must have preceded the words just cited. From this, it is truly to be concluded that the serpent must have been a very beautiful animal, very close to the **human figure**, since the woman engaged with it so; indeed, the serpent must have been entirely a **human** (yet without the immortal Adamite body and spirit), substantialized out of this animal world and formed very beautifully and perfectly. It was this serpent's **flesh and blood** that Adam and his wife later had to take on as their punishment. This serpent, however, as its own punishment, was robbed of its speech, as well as its hands and <margin>148</margin> **feet**, and was transfigured into such a **worm** (now called the serpent). # Concerning the Sabbath Rest.

When man was cast out of Eden onto this earth, cursed through his sin, GOD the LORD rested on the seventh day from all that he had made, thus concluding and completing a great number in Seven; and this seventh part or day he blessed and sanctified for a rest of body and soul, as may be seen in Exodus 20:11, so that man, after his six days of toil, labor, and the sweat of his brow, might again have a refreshment for body and soul. For because man did not remain in Eden during this seventh day of holy Divine rest, he also did not essentially enjoy the incomprehensible rest and Divine blessing of the seventh day with the holy spirits in the Divine Light. However, so that his desire to become a partaker of this peculiar Rest and Sabbath might be kindled within him, GOD the LORD gave him this seventh day or portion of a time—namely, of a week—in which not only to rest from his external hardship and labor, but also to refresh his spirit and soul again through Divine contemplation, so that he might thus visibly have a foretaste of the eternal rest and Sabbath in GOD through Christ.

§. 2. Furthermore, in this span of seven days as a week, the entire course and completion of all times appointed by GOD is perfectly prefigured. In Matthew 6:34 it is written: *It is enough that each day has its own trouble* <note>original: "Es ist genug, daß ein jeglicher Tag seine eigene Plage habe"</note>. Namely, just as man finds his particular hardship and trouble on each day and is freed from the same through sleep (as a symbol of death), so he is freed from hardship and the clinging nature of sin at the end of his days through death; and in the same, as if in a nightly sleep, he is refreshed, prepared, and made wakeful for the final Seventh Time as his Sabbath, to see the same in a joyful state with Christ his Savior, as the heavenly Adam, who has brought back down everything that was lost in the first Adam.

§. 3. And just as each day has its own trouble, so also each day or period of the great "World-Week" <note>A concept in mystical theology where the history of the world is divided into seven great epochs corresponding to the seven days of creation.</note> has its appointed troubles, along with intervening times of refreshment as nights of rest, so that nature in its hardship under the curse must not succumb entirely, until those Sabbath-times or Seven-

Yet every man may believe concerning this what he pleases, if only he earnestly endeavors to be raised up again from the Fall through Christ, and to be renewed according to the image of Him who created us. To which we hereby heartily exhort the favorable reader, wishing to have given occasion for further reflection upon these things.

# On the Origin and Generation of Sulphur.

It has been shown that this solar and lunar wonder-fire △ <note>The triangle △ is the symbol for Fire, here representing the "Sulphur of Nature" or the vital spark</note> or Balsam is to be found in all creatures as their soul. However, this was not done to strengthen the delusions of alchemists and other "coal-killers" <note>German: "Kohlen-Mörder"; a derogatory term for amateur alchemists who wasted vast amounts of charcoal on failed experiments</note> who wish to persuade the world through their folly that—because a tiny seed of gold may be shown to exist in the lesser metals and minerals—these metals should have become gold if they had reached their full maturation, like gold itself, and had not been prevented from doing so in their matrix <note>The "womb" or geological pocket where minerals develop</note> by coarse, foreign parts, thus becoming this or that lesser metal. In truth, however, they have missed the mark as far as heaven is from the earth.

> " For the Almighty GOD, out of His eternal providence and for the greater
> " glorification of His wondrous majesty, brought forth the diversity of
> " creatures, so that stockfish <note>Dried cod</note> should not be gold, nor 
> " herring be buttermilk; Crystal has no Jupiter ♃ <note>Tin</note>, nor does 
> " Venus ♀ <note>Copper</note> have marble or jasper;

and thus, Mars ♂ <note>Iron</note> was also not meant to be or become the Sun ☉ <note>Gold</note>; rather, for the sake of manifold use and benefit, the Sun ☉ was to be gold, and Mars ♂ was to be iron. But here I see a terrible army of "wind-catchers"—not those who transmute metals, but those who "transmute" themselves out of their senses—storming toward me. They wish to bombard us with countless examples of transformations that have occurred, to destroy our premise and confirm their own theorem: namely, that all metals could or should have become gold. Therefore, a bratwurst is a pair of Spanish trousers <note>A satirical German proverb used to highlight a non-sequitur or absurd logic</note>. It is not our current intention to offer these people a further reply; otherwise, we would soon help them out of their dream and show them the difference between reality and possibility, so that perhaps many might return to reason and the foundation of truth. They might then understand what a true transformation is—or more rationally, a separation of the pure from the coarse and impure. Those who have seen a true, rather than a sophisticated <note>In the sense of "sophistry" or deceptive</note> operation with their own eyes, will already understand what we are speaking of here.

§. 10. Above in Section 5, we stated that in this earthly lump or our terrestrial globe, there is no sun-dust in which Fire △ or Sulphur △ is not to be found; this requires no further explanation for reasonable people. Nor does it require proof that when this Fire △ or Sulphur △ is ignited, it rises in a flaming, very stinking, corrosive, destructive, and deadly light. Everyone also knows that the outward essence of this Fire △ consists of a stinking, slimy fatness, which allows much saltiness to be perceived as the beginning of this sliminess and of the <term>mercurial</term> ☿rial light <note>The light associated with Mercury, the principle of volatility and transformation</note>, as a cause for the revelation of the flame out of darkness and deadly fire. Furthermore, experience has shown that when this Sulphur △ is completely burned, a grain of Gold ☉ may then be drawn from its fatty or slimy remaining earthly essence; regarding this, we state this task clearly, plainly, and irreproachably to all the school-scholars—

### On the Origin and Production of Sulfur.

Everything that shines casts forth its rays, whether it possesses its light of itself or has borrowed it. In <note>Genesis 1:16</note> the Moon is called a light, with the addition: "the lesser [light]"; however, astronomical investigations prove that the Moon has no other light than that which it receives from being shone upon by the Sun, and thus the words of the holy text would only be understood with a distinction—namely, insofar as the Moon receives its light from the Sun. But the Holy Scripture says without any such distinction, in clear and plain words: **And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also, etc.** And thus the Moon should be a light to rule the night. The Holy Scripture is Truth, and in no place does it use such exaggerating figures of speech; it matters not how the Moon may be viewed through telescopes <note>original German: *Fern-Gläser*</note>. For just as in bright sunshine, at high noon, a small burning wax candle at a distance of 2,000 to 3,000 paces from our eyes cannot possibly be recognized as burning—even though one can actually see and recognize its body through a good perspective glass <note>An early type of telescope or spotting scope.</note>—it nevertheless is and remains a true, burning light; so, and in just such a manner, is the Moon also a true light, regardless of the fact that the stargazers <note>Astronomers</note> cannot recognize it as such. In this, however, it is by no means denied that it might receive its bright waxing and waning light from the Sun, as the center-point of all light known to us outside of the Heavenly Light, and that its own essential, indwelling light is thereby obscured and suppressed.

To be sure, a presumptuous wit <note>original German: *übersichtiger Klügling*—a term for someone who thinks they are more clever than they are.</note> will object and say: if the Moon indeed had its own independent light, one would surely have to recognize it at night on that part which is not being looked upon by the Sun, especially since the light of the bright day could then provide no reason for it to be hidden? Certainly, this objection has no small appearance of truth, especially when one bases it on experience and the evidence of telescopes; however, how far these are to be trusted in this matter is not our purpose here to investigate. Instead, we refer back to the Holy Scripture and to that which we have already said above concerning this. And above all this, it is as clear as day and obvious to all the world that when the Moon is new during clear weather, one can quite clearly distinguish and recognize its entire body, according to its whole circumference, by a dark fiery redness <note>Likely referring to "earthshine" or the "ashen light" of the moon, where the dark side of the moon is faintly visible.</note>. But the fact that the body of the Moon cannot always be so recognized by the eyes is caused by the increasing, powerful light of the Sun (☉). Thus, it remains firmly established by us, along with Holy Scripture, that the Moon (☽) in and of itself is a light (namely, a weak and dark one). <note>1 Corinthians 15:41</note> **There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars: for one star (✱) differeth from** another <note>Catchword: "another" (*andern*) indicates the start of the next page.</note>

# The Second Chapter.

Just as the sun makes a seed thrown into the <term>earth<note>symbol: 🜃</note></term> first swell through the first warmth of spring, then sprout in the form of a grass; further, through stronger heat, pulls it up into a hard stalk; thirdly, awakens the flower and the seed within it; and fourthly and finally, how it ripens and hardens this seed through the final degree of heat so that it becomes capable of infinite multiplication—whoever, we say, has learned this sufficiently will perfectly understand how to give the ripening to this red dust <term>Aphar<note>A Hebrew term often used in alchemy to refer to "dust" or "fine earth," specifically the "red earth" from which the first human was supposedly formed.</note></term>. and just as the lover of this art must learn these degrees simply from nature, he must likewise learn his <term>fire<note>symbol: 🜂</note></term> and oven from nature. # Chapter Three.

### [Of the Nature and Use of Earthly Sulfur]

That sulfur <note>original: "🜍"</note> inflicts damage upon silver <note>original: "☽"</note> is known to everyone; but what a certain sulfur <note>original: "🜍"</note>—which Nature has coagulated merely in common water <note>original: "🜄"</note>—is capable of doing to fine gold <note>original: "☉"</note>, and how it transforms the gold <note>original: "☉"</note> into an excellent red salt <note>original: "🜔"</note>, is not something everyone knows. Nor will everyone find this sulfur <note>original: "🜍"</note>, which is called "contrary to the common order."

§. 14. In the first part concerning salt <note>original: "🜔"</note>, we considered the **pebble-stones**; we must here make a brief mention of them once more, though without describing their distinct varieties, as such a task would be impossible. Their wonderful creation has already been discussed in the first part regarding salt <note>original: "🜔"</note>; here we wish only to mention those stones which one is accustomed to encounter frequently in very high mountains, and which are often composed of many thousands of small stones of all sorts of colors. Many thousands of people see this, but the smallest portion of them understands the cause. We do not wish to quote what is reported here and there by the <note>original: "Auctoribus"</note> authors. He who knows the cause of the earth's firmness, and why bricks (even if they are often burned from an entirely black earth) become so beautifully red through the fire <note>original: "🜂"</note>, will also easily grasp the cause of the "baking together" of so many pebbles in coarse sand, and often in a whitish, loamy earth. In particular, he will understand why the sulfur <note>original: "🜍"</note> of mercury <note>original: "☿"</note> is coagulated into such a high red.

The **soap-boiler's trade** shows us how, through an alkaline lye, all fattiness (which is fundamentally nothing other than a pure sulfur <note>original: "🜍"</note>) curdles together and becomes a hard soap. This undeniable mechanical proof should overturn many a person's <note>original: "grillichte Principia Physica"</note> whimsical physical principles and point them toward the foundation of Nature. However, because the imagination—especially that which is sired by presumed high scholarship—is an incurable evil (as one sees almost daily at the gates among those <term>fools<note>Likely referring to the mentally ill or "fools" who were often found near city gates or in public hospitals, laboring under delusions of grandeur.</note></term> who imagine they are this or that personage), so it goes with most people in their once-conceived opinions. 

Yet we say once again, that this lowly and humble comparison to soap-boiling contains more within it than many are able to think. If many understood what we intended to point out herewith, the **smelting works** would not proceed so "executioner-like" with the poor ores, but would instead learn to better understand their <term>fluxes<note>Materials added to the ore to promote melting and remove impurities.</note></term>. But here, many poor souls will immediately bare their teeth at us and mockingly ask: where are they to get all the salt <note>original: "🜔"</note> and mercury <note>original: "☿"</note> in order to help the antimonial <note>original: "♁lichten"</note> ores according to our teaching (as they imagine it)? 

But not so hasty to turn, you poor little animals! The Creator alone knows how to lead you to the necessary fodder, for not everything that is green is a good <term>feeding<note>original: "Atzung"; archaic term for food or bait for animals.</note></term> for you. Parables indeed indicate the matter, but for that reason they are not the matter itself; a principle that many <note>original: "Gottes-Gelehrten"</note> theologians would likewise find highly necessary to take to heart.

-># On the Nature, Utility, and Use of Earthly Sulfur.<-

There is a great difference between the shadow and the essence. Learn the nature and its produced species well; then you will rightly understand where we are pointing, to your own honor and the benefit of your neighbor.

§. 15. That common <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "🜍"; sulfur was often associated with the soul or the combustible principle of a substance.</note> cannot be easily dissolved by any liquid substance is known to almost everyone. However, it is not quite so common to know that one can easily and completely dissolve it into a red juice within a lye that has been sharpened to the highest degree by lime (one will surely understand what we are talking about <note>This likely refers to a caustic potassium or sodium hydroxide solution made with quicklime.</note>), and afterwards, through a certain <term>menstruum</term> <note>A solvent; from the Latin "menstruus," referring to the alchemical idea of a solvent acting over a cycle of time.</note>, extract a tincture or balsam from this solution. This is easy to prepare, provided one knows the correct lye as well as the solvent, which in no way wishes to unite or mix with the lye. Furthermore, once one has brought this balsam to the thickness of honey, and then cooks or "cements" a volatile <term>silver</term> <note>original: "☽" (Luna); "volatile silver" refers to a chemically prepared or purified form of the metal.</note> within it according to the degrees of nature—or whatever else one wishes to call it according to the **art of gold-making**—one might hope for no small pleasure from this work. What then would the heavenly wonder-<term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "🜍"</note> described above in Chapter II not achieve, if a true artist were to proceed with it according to the humble way of nature? But know this: if you do not know how to prepare the aforementioned volatile <term>silver</term> <note>original: "☽"</note> well, and how to make it bodily <note>To "make bodily" means to reduce it back to a solid, metallic state from a solution or vapor.</note> again after the cooking, you will have nothing but loss from it. He who knows the art should not betray the master, lest both fall into contempt; for this work is in itself humble and small, yet it has something great behind it, only that this work requires much time and patience.

§. 16. Enough has already been said to one practiced in <term>sulfur</term> <note>original: "🜍"</note>; but as for others who think they have already "smelled this pepper" <note>A German idiom meaning to have an inkling or a bit of experience with something difficult.</note>, we assure them that they will hardly reach this little side-stream without a faithful guide, as such a thing may be called by many names—yet quite clearly—even if it is not understandable to everyone.

§. 18. # On the Nature, Utility, and Use of Earthly Sulfur.

Soot (which, because it is a <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍. In alchemy, sulfur represents the principle of combustibility and soul.</note> that is very harmful to ores, seems a bit absurd) works wonders with volatile ores; the cause of this will be easily understood by one practiced in nature. However, he who does not understand the correct practice with soot should leave it be, unless he wishes to carry away harm, shame, mockery, and scorn instead of benefit. Chimney soot’s closest relative <note>likely referring to lampblack or a similar carbon-based substance.</note> likewise does its part with volatile ores, provided that one knows how to assist both the one and the other with their necessary <term>mercuriality</term> <note>The quality of being volatile, fluid, or transformative, associated with the principle of Mercury.</note>. But enough of this, as we do not wish to act as a smelter here; yet we must still remember that common <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> is able to increase <term>copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀</note> in a certain way. Namely, when one uses a quarter part <term>copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀</note> and one part <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, the <term>copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀</note> then becomes a "stone" <note>likely a metal matte or crude sulfide ore</note> with half of the <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>. After this stone is first made black through true science and then further turned into copper, it will show that the <term>copper</term> <note>original symbol: ♀</note> has received a considerable increase from the <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>; and this work can give a seeker much useful information.

§. 19. Above in §. 13, we mentioned the calcination <note>original: "Verzunderung," the process of heating a metal until it scales or turns to ash.</note> of <term>gold</term> <note>original symbol: ☉</note> and <term>silver</term> <note>original symbol: ☽</note>; now we wish to mention <term>antimony</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note> with just a few words. When one calcinates it, its combustible <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> departs along with the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note>, which is the cause of the <note>original: "vis emetic:"</note> **emetic power** <note>The ability to induce vomiting, a common trait of antimonial preparations.</note> of <term>antimony</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note>, and its golden <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> remains alone. What is then to be performed with it in the <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: △</note> (especially if one knows how to catch its combustible <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> along with the <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> during calcination)—namely, when the same is reunited with its separated parts after they have been washed by <term>antimony's</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note> own vinegar—we do not wish to mention at this time, because the vinegar of <term>antimony</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note> is required for it, the preparation of which is not known to everyone.

§. 20. But <term>antimony</term> <note>original symbol: ♁</note> is not alone in being endowed with a noble <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>; <term>iron</term> <note>original symbol: ♂</note> also has an excellent and quite fixed <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note>, and most of its substance consists of this; of its <term>mercury</term> <note>original symbol: ☿</note> there is very little, and of <term>salt</term> <note>original symbol: ⊖</note> it has somewhat more. The <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> of <term>iron</term> <note>original symbol: ♂</note> is of excellent quality, both in medicine and in alchemy. Many medicines are prepared from it, but what a miserable mess it often is, the poor patients experience to their greatest discomfort; its <note>original: "Crocus solubilis"</note> **soluble crocus** <note>A chemical preparation of iron, usually an oxide, used as a tonic.</note> and **tincture** are the best medicines made from it. Were medicine our profession, we could share many curious preparations with the seekers here; but the Scripture says: *Let no one reach into another’s office!* Therefore, we leave such things to those whose profession it is. In external injuries, its red, sugar-sweet **balsam** (provided it has no foreign additions) is a wonder; its **ore** <note>original: "Minera"</note>, if it be pure, yields the very best balsam. This balsam of <term>sulfur</term> <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> is also prepared for internal use, performing its part with great praise. <term>Iron</term> <note>original symbol: ♂</note> also has a wondrous magnetic power in itself, and a true wonder-magnet can be prepared from it; but that does not belong in this chapter. But he to whom the **love affairs** of **iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> are known, and how he is inclined to cool his heat with all sorts of lowly folk, can easily introduce a **harlot** <note>A metaphor for a less noble additive or flux that attracts the iron away from the precious metal.</note> to him. Whoever does not rightly understand this, however, should let **iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note> be during smelting; otherwise, he will have to scratch himself mightily behind the ears <note>An idiom for being in a state of regret, confusion, or frustration.</note>. Common **sulfur** <note>original symbol: 🜍</note> is an enemy of **iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>; if a **Vitriolic** <note>original: "Sig-rialiſches," likely a corruption of "Vitriolic" (sulfate-based).</note> essence comes to its aid, neither its bravery nor its armor can protect it. But he—**iron** <note>original symbol: ♂</note>—transforms himself entirely into the flesh and blood of **Venus** <note>Copper</note> out of love for her as soon as she entices him to enter into her bath with her and to sweat properly therein. [Crea]tures are simply composed of the elements or <term>secondary principles</term> <note>original: "Principiis secundariis"; in alchemical philosophy, these are the four elements (Earth, Water, Air, Fire) which proceed from the three primary principles of Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury</note> proportionally according to their kind; just as fish and all poultry are from the element of Water; all animals, cattle, and creeping things are from the Earth. Thus, they actually have no part in the Darkness, except insofar as Man, through his Fall, brought the curse upon all of nature, while drawing damnation upon himself alone. Consequently, Man has within himself far more of the principles of Darkness and Damnation than all other creatures. Conversely, within this shell of Darkness, Damnation, and Corruption, Man also possesses—above all other creatures—the noble heavenly jewel of Spirit, Soul, and Body from Eden, namely "dust from the earth," locked within. Therefore, the flesh and blood of a man united with GOD, through heavenly <term>radiation</term> <note>original: "Radiation"; used here to mean a divine emanation or spiritual glow</note>, is much more glorious, excellent, and useful than that of a man walking according to the impulses of Satan and the principles of Darkness.

We see a likeness of this in the glorious radiance of Moses, when he had been with GOD the Lord on Mount Sinai for forty days and nights; no human eye could endure his excellent glow, even though he had not yet laid aside his elemental essence and still required food and drink like all other men. Furthermore, we see that the dead bones of the excellent man of GOD, Elisha, still worked wonders and awakened a deceased man once more (2 Kings 13:21)—a glorious symbol that the death of JESUS Christ shall give life again to all who have blessedly fallen asleep.

On the other hand, it is of an entirely different nature with the possessed man in the region of the Gadarenes (Mark 5), who stayed only in the stinking, unclean tombs, led a loathsome, desolate, dark life, and was a dwelling for a legion of devils. His flesh and blood, before redemption through JESUS Christ, would have been highly harmful and dangerous to the body and soul of another human being. This is well known to all sorcerers, who exercise their sorceries upon humans and cattle through such devilish mummial <term>subjects</term> <note>original: "Subjecta"; the physical medium or vessel used to carry a spiritual influence</note>; these may be healed again in no other way than through pure, true Divine <term>Magic</term> <note>original: "Magie"; here referring to "Theurgia" or high spiritual science, contrasted with "Goetia" or dark sorcery</note>. For this, something mummial is specifically required from certain people, through which the harm done can be brought back upon the neck of the sorcerer, so that even Satan with all his cunning cannot prevent it—provided one well understands the fire of judgment and the human <term>Mumia</term> <note>original: "Mumia"; the vital life-force or balsamic essence residing in the physical body</note>. This, however, is a mystery which, for certain reasons, cannot and will not be mentioned.

For it appears that this prophecy occurred during the time of the Babylonian King Phul Belochi <note>Likely referring to Tiglath-Pileser III, called "Pul" in the Bible, who reigned over Assyria and Babylon</note> (who heard Jonah’s preaching of repentance and turned to a certain, though not perfect, repentance); therefore he did not go into Bor, but into Sheol.

§. 13. Thus it is manifest that those kept in Sheol may be called forth and can appear. We must nevertheless remind the reader that in Sheol there are different levels or circles, where one is always more fortunate than the other; the opposite of which is to be understood regarding Bor, the prison. To this we answer briefly: a spirit is a dense, hard light, but the light is an invisible **Fire** <note>represented by the alchemical symbol △</note>, **NB.** a beam of the eternal Godhead; the clothing of a spirit, however, according to its form, is a sulfurous, volatile **Salt** <note>represented by the alchemical symbol ⊖; in this context, it refers to the "body" of the spirit-soul</note>; and therefore a spirit is an incomprehensible wonder-creature. Whoever truly understands this description will have a great light kindled for them in all these writings, and will understand much more clearly what we mean by the first outflow of Divine Majesty, from which all things were created, and which we have called a unity in the threefold—namely **Salt** <note>⊖</note>, **Fire** <note>△</note>, and **Mercury** <note>☿; together these represent the *Tria Prima* or three primary substances of the universe</note>. For every man remains in his form until he appears after his resurrection in his glorified body, according to the measure of the glorified body of Jesus Christ, which is well worth noting for certain reasons.

## The Fourth Chapter.

§. 16. Regarding the recently cited text from Luke, it would not be out of place to make a brief mention of the dispute between the two Protestant churches, where one comes quite close to the doctrine of Transubstantiation <note>The Catholic belief that the bread and wine literally become the body and blood of Christ.</note>, while the other, on the contrary, goes perhaps a little too far in the opposite direction. The former wishes to maintain that the Lord Christ, through the omnipotence of His divinity, stepped into the midst of His disciples through the closed door which was opened to Him. They do this so that their doctrine of *in, with, and under* <note>original: *cum & sub*. This refers to the Lutheran doctrine of Consubstantiation, where Christ is physically present alongside the bread and wine.</note> might be better defended. They do not consider that there is a very great difference—in terms of movement and effect—between a spirit and a glorified body such as Christ the Lord had at that time. To present this somewhat understandably through a comparison, take a good <term>Sal Armoniacum</term> <note>original: $\ominus$ Armoniacum. This is Sal ammoniac, a salt used in alchemy and early chemistry.</note>, and from it prepare a perfectly rectified Spirit, and from the remaining salt, according to the art, create a pure, clear glass, as a likeness of our glorified, translucent body. Fill this glass with its Spirit, but leave it unsealed; then place this glass into another glass or vessel, covered simply with paper at the top. You will then find in fact that the volatile Spirit will gradually evaporate through, but its transparent body (namely the glass) in which it was poured cannot pass through in the same way. This comparison is indeed taken from a spirit and a body that are quite coarse and far too material when compared to heavenly things; nevertheless, an enlightened eye will be able to see into the true mystery through this.

§. 17. That the Lord Christ already possessed a glorified body at that time is something no upright theologian <note>original: *Theologus*</note> would likely doubt; otherwise, such a person (provided his brain is not displaced by a stubborn prejudice) would be made to blush with shame by the passages in Mark 16:19 and Acts 1:9. Nevertheless, Christ the Lord says to His disciples, when they were under the impression that they were seeing a ghost: "Touch me and see me well; for a spirit has not flesh and bone, as you see that I have." From this, it is indeed irrefutable that even a glorified body remains tangible, and consequently requires a specific location according to its full extension and dimension. Otherwise, one would have to claim, contrary to St. Paul's clear words, that Christ had not yet been glorified at that time. But how false this is, the Apostle declares irrefutably in 1 Corinthians 15:42, which also points to what Christ says in His Passion Sermon in John 17:5. These good gentlemen would have no need to invent such a strange "penetration" through closed doors for the body of our Savior, if they would only wipe the dust of the schools <note>original: *Schul-Staub*; a metaphor for dry, pedantic academic learning that blinds one to spiritual truth.</note> from their eyes and consider the passages in Luke 24:16 and John 21:4 without their usual, shabby logical tricks.

This is because Satan, through his fall, was cast out from the circle of all spiritual and physical creatures, so that in and of himself he no longer possesses even the slightest form of any heavenly or earthly creature. Rather, according to his devilish form and essence—as the center of **God's** wrath and of the dark, cold **wrath-nature** <note>original: *Grimm-Ars*. Likely a variation of *Grimm-Art*, referring to a nature characterized by divine fury or the 'wrathful fire' described in theosophy.</note>—he is unbearable to all creatures.

It is not that they take on a body which they then abandon after the appearance, as the angels do. Instead, they have and retain—as mentioned above—a fleeting **rectified spirit** <term>Spir. rectific.</term>, an **ethereal vehicle** <term>Vehiculum</term> (or whatever the school-philosophers, puffed up with empty words, might otherwise care to call it). But why they appear—and often in the clothing in which they walked during their life—shall now be explained.

# The Fourth Chapter.

§. 22. Now, concerning this question: why do ghosts or spirits appear in certain places and only at certain times? (For we are not speaking here of the kind of ghosts mentioned in the <term>Book of Wisdom 17:3, 4, 15</term> <note>A book of the biblical Apocrypha. Therefore, before we prove this, it is necessary to speak of the substantiality of true faith, not in the way it is typically described in the schools. Paul describes faith in <term>Hebrews 11:1</term> thus: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, and the evidence of things not seen." Paul lists many mighty effects of this faith throughout this entire chapter, and *NB* in verse 27 he says: "By faith he (Moses) left Egypt, not fearing the wrath of the king: for he endured, as seeing him who is invisible." Verse 34: "Quenched the violence of <note>original symbol: $\Delta$, fire</note> fire, escaped the edge of the sword, out of weakness were made strong, waxed valiant in fight, turned to flight the armies of the aliens," etc. Thus, according to Paul's teaching, faith is a firm assurance within a person of that which he does not see or has not seen; or, a true **impression of the imagination** <term>impressio imaginationis</term> of those things that are not seen, as if they were truly and actually being seen. A blind man does not see the sun with his physical eyes, yet through his **imaginative power** <term>per vim imaginativam</term> <note>The faculty of the soul that forms internal images and grasps spiritual realities.</note> he is entirely assured that it lights the day, just as if he saw it physically. A covered concave mirror cannot receive the sun's rays and reflect them back; it is exactly the same with our souls and minds. So long as a person does not cast out and banish everything earthly from himself, the Holy Spirit cannot work, nor can the person reflect his imagination back into God—which is to say, he cannot believe.

Through this radiation, the object is grasped according to its entire substance and is imprinted and incorporated into our mind. From this, a person receives a perfect assurance of the essence of the object—that it is exactly so and not otherwise. With true faith, however, and spiritual <term>Imagination</term> <note>In this context, "Imagination" (from the Latin *imago*) does not mean "making things up," but rather the soul's faculty for forming an internal "image" or representation of spiritual truths.</note> and illumination upon spiritual things, the situation is as previously mentioned, with the difference that the imagination is here often guided and led to invisible things through visible ones.
