Furthermore, the circumstances of a matter also lead our imagination or faith so that one can be assured and certain of this or that—that is, one can believe it. Thus, we firmly believe that the <term>Great Mogul</term> <note>The Mughal Emperor of India, used here as a common 18th-century example of someone known to exist through report despite never being seen personally.</note> in India must be a rational human being and not an elephant, even though we have never seen him; this is because humans are governed by humans and not by irrational animals. Since we are bound to believe this firmly according to the circumstances, we simultaneously form an image of his great power, splendor, and glory, etc. Conversely, our imagination cannot possibly conceive—that is, believe—that the surface of the great world-ocean is divided into mighty kingdoms, principalities, and lordships, inhabited by various peoples and ruled by powerful potentates, just like our earth; for this runs contrary to the nature of that element. Therefore, faith is founded solely upon those invisible things that are real and true, and yet to come; namely, that such things are seized by the rays of our <term>Imagination</term> and impress a perfect image upon our spirit and soul, so that we need no longer have the slightest doubt about the matter. This is what it means to believe firmly in something, and thus faith is nothing other than a firm grasping of invisible things through our <term>Imagination</term> or an impression made by a mental image. However, the more a person's <term>Imagination</term> is filled and veiled with vanity, the less capable it will be to shine into spiritual things, and through such illumination to sink into them and unite inseparably with them. For this reason, an ungodly person does not believe in the righteous vengeance and the strict judgment of **GOD**, because his <term>Imagination</term> only shines into sinful vanities, having <term>originated</term> <note>original: "geurständet," a term often used in mystical theology to describe the root or source from which a thing arises or "takes its standing."</note> from the Devil, and thereby mixes itself with Satan; whereas a pious person, with his whole <term>Imagination</term>, sinks into **GOD** as the original source of all perfect joy, peace, rest, and eternal delight of the soul—that is, he perfectly believes in the almighty **GOD**, as He has revealed Himself in His Word

# On the Condition of Man After His Death.

In my **Father’s house are many dwellings**, etc. <note>original: "Vatters Hause sind viel Wohnungen 2c." – A reference to John 14:2.</note> Namely: (1) The **forecourts of the Lord**, of which David speaks in Psalm 84; (2) **Abraham’s bosom**; (3) **Paradise**; (4) **The New Jerusalem**; (5) **The new heaven and the new earth**; (6) **Zion**; (7) **The Kingdom of God**. Thus, Christ promised the thief <note>The "Penitent Thief" crucified alongside Jesus.</note> in Luke 23:43 Paradise, though the latter had asked for the Kingdom—that is, the final degree of blessedness. For although he <term>imagined</term> <note>In this mystical context, "imagination" refers to the soul’s ability to focus its internal will and "form" itself around a spiritual reality.</note> himself into Christ and took hold of Him in faith, he nonetheless lacked the preparation of a long and earnest repentance required by God’s justice, since he had spent his life in pure wickedness until that very moment, as he confessed in verse 41 when he said to his companion: "for we receive what our deeds deserve," etc. But because he took hold of Christ through a powerful irradiation of His Spirit and believed that He was the Son of God—who would not remain in death and could therefore lead him out of it and free him from the anguish of hell—Christ accepted him into grace. He promised to take him into **Paradise** as the third degree of rest, which Christ Himself intended to occupy until His victorious ascension above the heaven of all heavens.

§. 26. In the second Epistle to the Corinthians 12:2, St. Paul says he was caught up into the **third heaven**, into Paradise. It does not follow from this that there are only three heavens or degrees of blessed rest; he merely says he was caught up as far as the third heaven, but did not reach the others, as is evident from the text. Furthermore, that dead boy whom Elijah raised <note>1 Kings 17</note>, and the one who returned to life through the dead bones of Elisha <note>2 Kings 13:21</note>, as well as the dead man at Nain raised by Christ <note>Luke 7</note>, the little daughter of the ruler of the synagogue <note>Luke 8</note>, and Lazarus called back from the grave <note>John 11</note>; likewise Tabitha raised by Peter <note>Acts 9</note> and the youth Eutychus made alive again by Paul <note>Acts 20</note>—all these, we say, stood only in the **first degree of rest**. They were in the first circles of the **forecourts of the house of the Lord** (Psalm 84 and 116), because their <term>imagination</term> or rapture reached no further. And of this, the Book of Wisdom says in Chapter 3:1, **"The souls of the righteous are in God's hand, and no torment touches them."** All these remain in a state of rest from which they can only return to this world and the circles of darkness through the power of God. (Therefore Abraham says to the rich man in Luke 16:26: "And besides all this, between us and you a **great gulf** is fixed," etc.) This is because their imagination (namely, their faith) had been immersed in God and united with Him.

Rather, it is a **gift of grace** through the most holy suffering and merit of Jesus Christ. For truly, the sinner must come to Christ through faith and repentance, whether it happens here or there, as we have proven thus far from Holy Scripture. ## Of the State of Man After His Death.

"Truly, I say to you, you will by no means come out from there until you have paid the last penny," <note>original: "Amen, ich sage dir, du wirst mit nichten von dannen heraus kommen, bis du auch den lezten Heller bezahlest"; see Matthew 5:26.</note> This is not to be interpreted as if we wished to attribute any merit to the corrupted and damnation-worthy creature; no, in truth! Rather, we understand these words according to the foundation of Holy Scripture in this way: namely, that the sinner in those places (which are called "the prison" by Christ) must break through from the dark places into the light through the effect of the Holy Spirit. This happens through much more indescribable anguish and soul-distress than he would have had to endure in this life, and through an anxious, repentant wrestling in faith regarding all sins, even the very smallest committed. And this is then absolutely a grace and mercy of the Father in the merit of Jesus Christ, and not a deserved reward for the sinner because of his own satisfaction, as is so heretically charged against us by the <term>heresy-hunters</term> <note>original: "Ketzermachern"; literally "heresy-makers," a derisive term for dogmatic theologians who label any differing opinion as heresy.</note>. But concerning Christ’s words in Mark 3:29, namely: **"Whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is guilty of eternal judgment."** It may well seem that our opponents can construct from these words an eternal, infinite judgment that lasts as long as God Himself, especially from the phrase: **"never has forgiveness."** However, anyone who has properly grasped the meaning of "Eternal" <note>original: "Ewiglich"; in this mystical tradition, "eternal" often refers to a long age or "aeon" rather than infinite time.</note> according to the sense of the Scripture will also understand that this "eternity" will finally end along with the kingdom of Satan, when it shall be said in Revelation 22:3: **"There shall be no more curse;"** <note>original: "Es wird kein Verbanntes mehr seyn"; literally, "There will be no more banned/accursed thing."</note> which has already been explained clearly enough in the preceding text and shall be further addressed as the opportunity arises.

...and Section 3 of this chapter. That the earthly or elementary body consists of <term>Salt</term> <note>Original symbol: 🜔</note>, <term>Sulfur</term> <note>Original symbol: 🜍</note>, and <term>Mercury</term> <note>Original symbol: ☿</note> requires no proof among the knowledgeable. The <term>Salt</term> <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary substances of alchemy: Salt (stability/body), Sulfur (combustibility/soul), and Mercury (volatility/spirit).</note> is and remains the most solid and constant part in the dissolution of all created beings; it refines itself in <term>Sulfur</term> ever higher, more beautiful, and more transparent. In this earthly <term>Salt</term> is hidden the super-earthly heavenly <term>Salt</term>—the "dust from the earth," or the body indestructible for all eternity—which, however, cannot appear or be revealed until the Day of Resurrection. This is undeniably testified by Paul in 1 Corinthians 15, where in verse 35 he raises the question:

> But someone might say: how are the dead raised, and with what kind of body do they come? Answer v. 36. You fool! That which you sow does not come to life unless it dies. v. 37. And what you sow is not the body that is to be, but a bare grain, etc. v. 44. It is sown a natural body, and it is raised a spiritual body. There is a natural body, and there is also a spiritual body.

These sun-bright sayings need no explanation; rather, it is revealed through them that with our natural, corruptible body, a spiritual, incorruptible body is also buried. This spiritual body, created from spiritual elements or "beginnings," alone shall rise again; just as the wheat grain placed in the earth does not return in the same form, but pushes forth a body completely unlike itself, as its stalk, ear, blossom, and fruit prove. But why must the glorious incorruptible body rest with the corruptible in the grave, and remain there until its resurrection? This cause must be sought in the first man, Adam. §. 7. Now John continues, and reports the reason why the devil should lie bound and imprisoned for 1,000 years: namely, so that he might no longer deceive the heathen <note>The "nations" or "gentiles"</note>, etc. Here it seems as if he speaks simply of those who do not recognize the true God and Christ whom He has sent. ...Christ the LORD will appear in His kingdom, a great portion will be converted; as Christ the LORD Himself says in Matthew 24:14 concerning His kingdom, namely: *And this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness against all nations, and then the end will come.* Paul says in Romans 11:25: *For I do not want to keep this from you, dear brothers! However, how and in what manner this great conversion of both the aforementioned various types of <term>Gentiles</term> <note>original: Heyden; referring to non-believing nations</note>, and especially of the Jews, will occur, cannot be said by any creature, as the Holy Scripture mentions no specific way in any place, but only speaks of the aforementioned general conversion. A specific time is set for this cruel and terrifying persecution, as can be read in Daniel 12:7, namely, that it would last for *a time, times, and half a time.* In Revelation 11 and 13, it is mentioned that this would last 42 months, a term which many diligent men wish to understand as three and a half years, namely, the amount that 42 months equals in years; therefore, in Daniel 12:7, it must mean to them: one time, two times, and half a time. 

But if one can prove that the word <term>Moadim</term> <note>Hebrew: מועדים; meaning "appointed times" or "seasons"</note> found in the original text is in the dual form and speaks only of "two" times (which, according to the properties of the language, cannot be easily proven), then we would gladly accept it; otherwise, it simply remains as <term>Piscator</term> <note>Johannes Piscator (1546–1627), a prominent Reformed theologian known for his Bible translations and commentaries</note> rightly translated it, namely, "certain times": so that the duration of this cruel persecution, regarding both its beginning and its length, remains a secret number (as mentioned in §. 9), and consequently will not be recognized before its fulfillment. Furthermore, at this coming of Christ to His glorious kingdom, the fulfillment of the parable of the ten virgins—of whom five were wise and the others foolish—is to be expected. Concerning all of this, a more detailed and extensive account shall follow below in the discourse on the Revelation of Jesus Christ.

# The Fifth Chapter.

### That by the sound of the trumpet only the elect from all four parts of the world shall be gathered (to the Holy Land, Ezekiel 34:8 at the end).

After the judgment has been held, John continues and says: "And I also saw the souls of those who had been beheaded" (namely, in their various heavenly dwellings, as the sequence of the resurrection clearly explains) "for the testimony of Jesus," etc. <note>This refers to Revelation 20:4.</note> These came to life again and reigned with Christ for the thousand years. From the aforementioned text, one sees that those who will rise shall be: (1.) the martyrs and blood-witnesses of Christ; and then (2.) those who did not worship the beast and its image, and did not receive its marks—namely, the beast which "was and is not, and yet is," Revelation 17:8. Its "image" refers not to its physical form, but just as Nebuchadnezzar had his image <note>A reference to the golden statue King Nebuchadnezzar forced his subjects to worship in Daniel 3.</note>, so here too, it refers to those who did not worship the beast’s wooden, bronze, silver, and gold images and the mute oil-idols <term>oil-idols: likely a derogatory reference to the veneration of anointed statues or icons of saints</term> of both pious and evil men. There are almost more of these than stars in the sky, for one can hardly imagine anything that does not have such an idol as its patron; indeed, even the army of the beast could not count them all. Before these images all peoples, nations, and tongues fall down, just as they did before Nebuchadnezzar’s image in Daniel 3:7. These people shall not rise, but shall be kept until the final general judgment. But those who did not worship the beast’s image, nor accepted any of its marks, these are the ones who shall partake in the first resurrection and Christ’s 1,000-year kingdom.

## Chapter VII.

## Of the Torment of the Damned.

->§. 1.<-

After a final death sentence has been pronounced upon a criminal prisoner, he is handed over to the executioner <note>original: *Scharfrichter*</note> to have it carried out. Likewise, after the sentence has been spoken to all the godless on the Day of the Last Judgment by Christ Jesus—the judge of all the living and the dead—they shall, as heard in the previous chapter, be handed over to the devils for all manner of torment and torture. But in what shall this torment and torture actually consist? There is much dispute about this, and many are of the opinion that because the devil is an entirely spiritual substance, he cannot be harmed by any material <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note>. Similarly, they believe the godless would not be able to feel an elemental <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note> because Paul says in 1 Corinthians 15:44: 

> It is sown a natural body, and it is raised a spiritual body, etc. 

Regarding the opinion of the former: we have already reported in the first chapter, §. 12, in what manner the devils and the godless shall be tormented by this elemental and simultaneously spiritual <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note>, ignited by the breath of the Lord like a <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note> stream, as in Isaiah 30:33. This can be made even more understandable through the following comparison: if one were to place a proportionate amount of a highly rectified <term>spirit</term> <note>original: *Spiritus*; here referring to a highly concentrated, volatile substance like alcohol</note> into a large sphere, and at the same time placed, or could place, a <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note> of coals within it, the heat and power of the fire would cause the spirit within this circle to be distressed, pressed, driven about, and expanded everywhere; yet, it could never be destroyed for all eternity, as destruction runs contrary to the nature of a spirit. Thus, as long as the <term>fire</term> <note>original symbol: $\triangle$</note> in this circle had fuel to burn, the spirit locked within would be distressed and tortured.

# The Seventh Chapter.

§. 6. Regarding the humans deceived and damned by Satan, the horror of their torment can be partially seen from what has been previously stated. However, because humans consist of spirit, soul, and body (as shown above in Chapter 4, §. 32 <note>This refers to the tripartite view of human nature common in early modern theology and Hermetic philosophy, where humans are seen as more complex than purely spiritual beings like angels</note>), it is very easy to understand that their torment must be much more cruel and sensitive than that of the devils. This is because they shall feel and experience the fury of the hellish <term>$\triangle$</term><gloss>sulfur</gloss>-fire not only in their souls, as the devils do, but also in their damned bodies. They will suffer inconceivable pain: the heat from the <term>$\triangle$</term><gloss>fire</gloss>, and the cold from the tangible darkness, as Christ the Lord says in Matthew 8:12, 13:42, 22:13, 24:51, and 25:10; likewise in Luke 13:28: "And they shall cast them into the <term>$\triangle$</term><gloss>fire</gloss>-furnace: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth." In this regard, one should study with all diligence what was written above in Chapter 4, §. 3 and 7. The prophet Isaiah speaks in 34:9-10 and 66:24 of the damned and their torment with these words: "There shall its streams be turned into pitch, and its dust into <term>$\triangle$</term><gloss>sulfur</gloss>; yes, its land shall become burning pitch. It shall not be quenched night or day, but its smoke shall go up forever. And they shall go forth and look upon the dead bodies of the people who have rebelled against me: for their worm shall not die, and their <term>$\triangle$</term><gloss>fire</gloss> shall not be quenched, and they shall be an abomination to all flesh." — In Mark 9, Christ the Lord says three times (in verses 43, 45, and 47): "Where their worm does not die, and their <term>$\triangle$</term><gloss>fire</gloss> is not quenched." And in Revelation 14:11 <note>original: Apoc., referring to the Apocalypse of John</note> it says: "And the smoke of their torment will ascend for ever and ever: and they will have no rest, neither day nor night, who worship the beast and his image; and if anyone receives the mark of his name." Likewise in 19:3 <note>The source text says XIX, 2, but the quote follows from 19:3 and 19:20</note> and 19:20: "For her smoke rises up for ever and ever. # Of the Revelation of Jesus Christ etc.

XV. XVI. etc. In this time, which is divided into seven parts, is encompassed everything that shall happen to the church of Jesus Christ until the end of all times. It is evident from history that the seven churches in Chapters 2 and 3—namely those in Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea—were present in Asia at that time and were afflicted with the decline mentioned there. Generally, however, these serve to represent to Saint John seven epochs or periods of all churches throughout specific times, and what would occur with them until the end.

§ 4. The beginning is made with the Angel of the church at Ephesus. This church is highly praised and lauded in Chapter 2, verse 2, with these words: *I know your works* etc. In verses 3 and 4, however: *but I have something against you, namely that you have left your first love* etc. Furthermore, this period includes the opening of the first seal in Chapter 6, verse 2: namely the **rider on the white horse** with the bow and the crown, who went out to conquer and that he might overcome; just as many were overcome and became believers through the teaching of the Gospel in this period. Also fulfilled in this period is the trumpet of the first angel in Chapter 8, verse 7, which signifies the gruesome persecution under the Pagan Emperors up until **Constantine the Great** <note>original: "Constantinum M." referring to Constantinus Magnus</note>, foreshadowed by the words: *Then there was hail and fire, mingled with blood, and they were cast upon the earth, and the third part of the trees was burnt up, and all green grass was burnt up*; this indicates the multitude of martyrs, among the teachers as well as the entire congregation. Thus, contained within this is the first Apostolic Church, when the pure doctrine of Christ and his Apostles burned in the full <term>heat</term> <note>The original uses the Greek letter Δ (Delta), which in the alchemical and theological shorthand of this period often symbolized fire or divine heat.</note> of love, as is evident from the histories. Because the cruel persecutions affected all churches, they learned to pay heed to the Word through trials, and there was very little deviation from Apostolic purity until approximately the middle of this time—namely in the second <term>century</term> <note>original: "Seculo"</note>—when the leaders and elders in the churches rose up and assumed a ruling office. For example, in Alexandria after the death of Mark, the overseers or **bishops** were gradually elevated above the other elders, whereas previously one was like the other, and thus they were equals. From this arose jealousy, from jealousy hatred, and from hatred persecution and lack of love; thus the beginning of the subsequent clergy or the so-called <term>Hierarchy</term> <note>From the Greek "hieros" (sacred) and "arkhein" (to rule); here used to describe the transition from equal elders to a ranked priesthood.</note> was fathered. Therefore, Christ the LORD says: *you have left your first love, repent; if not, I will come and remove your lampstand from its place*; namely, take my grace and Spirit from you. In this, they are also praised for hating the works of the <term>Nicolaitans</term> <note>A group mentioned in Revelation 2:6 whose specific practices are debated by scholars, but were generally viewed by early Christians as heretical.</note>. This period is contained within the first 312 years after the birth of Christ our LORD, namely until the beginning of the reign of **Constantine the Great**, that is, until the year 312.

And the rest were terrified and gave glory to the GOD of heaven, just as the Baal-worshippers <note>original: "Baaliten"</note> did in 1 Kings 18:39: *The Lord is God, the Lord is God*; yet among these others, not the slightest mention is made of true repentance or improvement. v. 14. *The second woe is past; behold, the third woe comes quickly.*
